question: In a universe at eternal equilibrium, which random fluctuation is far likelier: a whole ordered galaxy, or one brain with false memories?
answer: One brain with false memories. Order that must appear all at once gets exponentially rarer with every extra piece, so a lone mind dreaming a past vastly outnumbers real galaxies. Boltzmann floated the fluctuation idea in 1895; today the lonely brain is the standard objection to it, since any observer's memories would almost surely be false.
move: Demand more order from chance and chance delivers it far less often.
trap: Picking the galaxy, because it is the world observers find around them.
source: Albrecht and Sorbo, Physical Review D, 2004
reference: Boltzmann, On Certain Questions of the Theory of Gases, Nature 51, 1895; Albrecht & Sorbo, Can the universe afford inflation?, Physical Review D 70, 2004
